text:
B: Oh, hello. Erm, can you hear me okay?
A: Yeah, yeah, I can hear you. Hiya.
B: Hi. I'm Joanne. Sorry, I'm never sure where to look on these things.
A: No, same. I'm Liam. I've been looking at me own face mostly, which isn't great.
B: Oh gosh, me too. Erm, where are you, roughly?
A: Doncaster. Bentley, sort of just north of town. You?
B: Basingstoke. Which nobody's ever excited about, so don't worry.
A: Never been. Heard of it though. It's got loads of roundabouts, right?
B: It has, yeah. That's basically all anyone knows. Erm, are you working today, or...?
A: No, I'm on nights, so this is sort of my morning really. I do shelf-stacking at a supermarket, four nights a week. Got up about one, had me tea. Well, it's more like breakfast but I call it tea. And then I logged on for this. So if I seem a bit slow that's why, do you know what I mean.
B: No, you seem fine. Gosh, I couldn't do nights. I'd be hopeless. Do you like it?
A: Yeah, it's alright. It's quiet. Nobody's on at you all the time. Just the lads and the radio and pallets. It's when they change the rota last minute that does me head in. What about you?
B: I'm a planner at the council. Erm, so planning applications, people's extensions, that sort of thing. I'm at home today, which is why there's a dog snoring behind me, sorry.
A: I saw that on your picture. What is it?
B: He's a cockapoo, Biscuit. He's quite old now and a bit anxious, so he follows me everywhere. Do you have any pets?
A: No, flat's too small really, and I'm out at night. I'd like a dog though. I walk a lot anyway, round Sandall Beat. There's a lake there. I'd have the walking sorted.
B: That sounds lovely, actually. I do the same loop twice a day with him. Same route every time. He gets upset if I change it.
A: Ha, he sounds like me.
B: Me too, to be honest. Erm, what do you do when you're not working, then?
A: Fishing mostly. Coarse fishing, just local ponds, the canal. Sit there on me own for a few hours. People think it's boring but it's not, it's sort of... you switch off. You're watching the float and you're not thinking about owt else. Bait's gone up a fortune, mind. Maggots are daft money now. Sorry, I'm rambling.
B: No, not at all. I think that's what the garden's meant to do for me, except I just stand there worrying about the slugs.
A: Do you grow stuff?
B: I try. Erm, I have a little veg bed and it's lovely until about August, and then I give up. Every year. I'm not sure that's very helpful, sorry.
A: No, that's alright. Me mam's the same with tomatoes. She gets loads of plants and then they all go mouldy.
B: Oh, that's exactly what happens. Did you do the puzzle bit at the start, by the way? I got completely stuck on it.
A: Yeah, I were rubbish at it. I just sort of guessed the last few. Thought I'd done it wrong.
B: Oh good. I mean, not good, but... I thought it was just me.
A: No, I reckon everyone struggled. Is Basingstoke nice for walking then, with the dog?
B: Erm, it's okay. There's the War Memorial Park near us, and at weekends we go out a bit further, sort of countryside. It's prettier than people think, honestly.
A: Might have to come down and see these roundabouts.
B: Ha, you'd be very disappointed.
A: Yeah... so, er, I think we're nearly out of time, are we?
B: Probably. It was really nice talking to you, Liam.
A: Yeah, you an' all.
